The average does not bound the hottest instant: because heat arrives in seconds during bursts but dissipates over minutes during recovery, the peak transient hotspot temperature during periodic pulsing strictly exceeds the time-averaged calculation,[^fn-math-thermal-peak] reaching `{python} ThermalBurst.t_peak_str` (above the ceiling) before the rise of $R(T)$ adds more. Average-power screening is optimistic, and a burst schedule is certified only against the transient hotspot trajectory.

[^fn-math-thermal-peak]: **Periodic steady-state thermal peak derivation**: In a periodic duty cycle of period $t_{\text{cycle}} = t_{\text{on}} + t_{\text{off}}$, summing the geometric series of heating and cooling exponentials yields the exact periodic peak temperature rise: $\Delta T_{\text{peak}} = P_{\text{peak}}\theta_{JA}\frac{1 - e^{-t_{\text{on}}/\tau_{\text{th}}}}{1 - e^{-t_{\text{cycle}}/\tau_{\text{th}}}}$. As $t_{\text{cycle}} \to 0$, this converges to the average-power screen ($D_{\text{cycle}} P_{\text{peak}}\theta_{JA}$); for finite burst durations, peak winding temperature strictly exceeds the average.

### Torque-speed operating envelopes and back-EMF roll-off {#sec-body-torque-speed-envelopes}

The burst calculation limits duration, while the back-EMF relation in @sec-body-electrical-time-constants limits torque at speed. A feasible maneuver must satisfy both. At low speed, the drive can supply the current needed for a burst, but the winding temperature limits how long it may do so. At higher speed, back-EMF consumes voltage headroom and can prevent that current from appearing at all. The torque-speed envelope in @fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope combines these constraints instead of treating peak torque as available at every speed and duration.

```{python}
#| label: body-torque-speed-envelope-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ TORQUE-SPEED ENVELOPE OF THE ARM'S JOINT MOTOR (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope in
# │          @sec-body-torque-speed-envelopes.
# │ Goal:    Show that torque is bounded by duty (S1 vs S3), by speed (back-EMF
# │          plus resistive drop), and by thermal history (burst horizon).
# │ Show:    (a) 1.25 / 4.05 N m, no-load 2,110 rpm, 1,942 rpm at rated and
# │          1,566 rpm at peak current; (b) cold 78.4 s and hot 43.1 s to 155 C.
# │ How:     Line-to-line voltage limit V = K_e,LL w + (sqrt(3)/2) R_TT i with
# │          K_e,LL = V_r / w_0 from the data sheet's no-load speed, i = tau/K_t
# │          (amplitude-invariant current, so the line drop is sqrt(3) i R_TT/2);
# │          inductance neglected. Panel (b) is ThermalBurst's first-order
# │          T(t) = T_inf - (T_inf - T_0) exp(-t/tau).
# │ Note:    The no-load speed is read here from the data sheet; promote it to
# │          Actuators.FramelessMotor.TQ_ILM70x18 (no_load_speed) when the
# │          registry next changes.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import math
import numpy as np
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim import viz
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_torque, fmt_voltage, fmt_int, check
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

class TorqueSpeedEnvelope:
    """Duty and voltage bounds on the TQ ILM 70x18 torque-speed plane."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    motor = Actuators.FramelessMotor.TQ_ILM70x18  # category: sourced (TQ-RoboDrive data sheet)
    tau_rated = motor.rated_torque  # category: sourced
    tau_peak = motor.peak_torque  # category: sourced (20 percent deviation from linearity)
    k_t = motor.torque_constant  # category: sourced
    r_tt = motor.terminal_resistance  # category: sourced (at 20 C)
    v_bus = motor.rated_voltage  # category: sourced
    n0 = 2110.0 * ureg.rpm  # category: sourced (data sheet Rev. 0414, star-serial no-load speed at U_r; theoretical)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    w0 = n0.to(radian / second)
    k_e = (v_bus / w0).to(volt * second / radian)  # line-to-line peak back-EMF constant

    def n_limit(tau, k_t=k_t, r_tt=r_tt, v_bus=v_bus, k_e=k_e):
        i = (tau / k_t).to(ureg.ampere)
        drop = (math.sqrt(3) / 2 * r_tt * i).to(volt)
        return ((v_bus - drop) / k_e).to(ureg.rpm)

    n_rated = n_limit(tau_rated)
    n_peak = n_limit(tau_peak)
    # Consistency: amplitude-invariant K_t implies K_e,LL = (2/sqrt(3)) K_t in SI
    k_e_from_kt = 2 / math.sqrt(3) * k_t.to(ureg.newton * meter / ureg.ampere).magnitude  # N m/A = V s/rad

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(k_e.magnitude - k_e_from_kt) / k_e_from_kt < 0.01, f"Data-sheet no-load speed and K_t disagree: K_e {k_e} vs {k_e_from_kt:.4f}")
    check(abs(n_rated.magnitude - 1942) < 1, f"Rated-current speed limit drifted: {n_rated}")
    check(abs(n_peak.magnitude - 1566) < 1, f"Peak-current speed limit drifted: {n_peak}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    tau_rated_str = fmt_torque(tau_rated, precision=2)
    tau_peak_str = fmt_torque(tau_peak, precision=2)
    v_bus_str = fmt_voltage(v_bus, unit=volt, precision=0)
    n0_str = f"{fmt_int(n0.magnitude)} rpm"
    n_peak_str = f"{fmt_int(round(n_peak.magnitude, -1))} rpm"
```

::: {#fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Torque, speed, and time on one joint motor**: (a) The TQ-RoboDrive ILM 70x18 of the arm's stand-in joint on its `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.v_bus_str` supply. Continuous duty $S_1$ extends up to the `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.tau_rated_str` rated torque; intermittent duty $S_3$ extends to the `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.tau_peak_str` peak. Both end where back-EMF plus the resistive drop uses up the supply, from the `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.n0_str` no-load speed down to `{python} TorqueSpeedEnvelope.n_peak_str` at peak torque; winding inductance, neglected here, pulls that boundary lower. (b) The winding temperature of the threefold-current burst of \ref{nbk-body-thermal-burst-limits}, a first-order rise toward `{python} ThermalBurst.t_inf_str` with $\tau_{\text{th}} =$ `{python} ThermalBurst.tau_str`. From ambient the burst reaches the `{python} ThermalBurst.t_limit_str` insulation class after `{python} ThermalBurst.t_cold_str`; from the continuous-duty equilibrium it gets there after `{python} ThermalBurst.t_hot_str`. The thermal values are illustrative, because the data sheet leaves them to the installation." fig-alt="Two panels. Panel a: torque against speed in revolutions per minute. A gray region below 1.25 newton meters is labeled S1 continuous, and an amber band from 1.25 to 4.05 newton meters is labeled S3 intermittent. A sloping line labeled voltage limit bounds both regions on the right, running from 2,110 revolutions per minute at zero torque down to about 1,570 at 4.05 newton meters. Panel b: winding temperature against time from 0 to 100 seconds. Two rising curves that bend over, one starting at 40 degrees Celsius and one at about 96 degrees, cross a red horizontal line at 155 degrees at about 78 and 43 seconds, marked with dots. A dashed gray line marks 140 degrees."}

```{python}
#| label: fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ TORQUE-SPEED ENVELOPE AND BURST HEATING (FIGURE)
# │ Context: @fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope
# │ Goal:    draw duty, voltage, and thermal-history bounds on one joint motor
# │ Show:    (a) S1/S3 regions under the voltage limit; (b) cold and hot bursts
# │ How:     TorqueSpeedEnvelope (body-torque-speed-envelope-calc) and
# │          ThermalBurst (body-thermal-burst-calc)
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import numpy as np
from mlsysim import viz
from mlsysim.core.units import *
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ┌── 5. PLOT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
E, T = TorqueSpeedEnvelope, ThermalBurst
R = viz.VOL4_ROLES
AMBER = "#D97706"
viz.set_book_style()
fig, (ax, bx) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.2), gridspec_kw=dict(wspace=0.32))

# (a) torque-speed plane
tr, tp = E.tau_rated.to(ureg.newton * meter).magnitude, E.tau_peak.to(ureg.newton * meter).magnitude
taus = np.linspace(0, tp, 50)
ns = np.array([E.n_limit(t * ureg.newton * meter).magnitude for t in taus])
n0, nr, npk = E.n0.magnitude, E.n_rated.magnitude, E.n_peak.magnitude
m1 = taus <= tr
ax.fill_betweenx(taus[m1], 0, ns[m1], color="#E2E8F0", lw=0)
ax.fill_betweenx(taus[~m1], 0, ns[~m1], color=AMBER, alpha=0.22, lw=0)
ax.plot(ns, taus, color=R["neutral"], lw=1.8)
ax.plot([0, nr], [tr, tr], color=R["neutral"], lw=1.0, ls="--")
ax.plot([0, npk], [tp, tp], color=AMBER, lw=1.4)
ax.text(nr * 0.42, tr * 0.45, "$S_1$ continuous", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=R["neutral"])
ax.text(npk * 0.45, (tr + tp) / 2, "$S_3$ intermittent", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color="#9A4F06")
ax.annotate(
    "voltage limit",
    xy=(E.n_limit(2.6 * ureg.newton * meter).magnitude, 2.6),
    xytext=(1900, 3.3),
    fontsize=8.5,
    color=R["neutral"],
    ha="left",
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=R["neutral"], lw=0.7),
)
for n, t, lab, ha in [(n0, 0, f"{n0:,.0f} rpm", "right"), (npk, tp, f"{npk:,.0f} rpm", "left")]:
    ax.plot(n, t, "o", color=R["neutral"], ms=4, zorder=5)
    ax.text(n + (-110 if ha == "right" else 40), t + 0.12, lab, ha=ha, va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=R["neutral"])
ax.set_xlim(0, 2500)
ax.set_ylim(0, tp * 1.15)
ax.set_yticks([0, 1, tr, 2, 3, 4, tp])
ax.set_yticklabels(["0", "1", f"{tr:.2f}", "2", "3", "", f"{tp:.2f}"])
ax.set_xlabel("Speed (rpm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Torque (N·m)")
ax.text(0.0, 1.03, "(a)", transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", ha="left", va="bottom")

# (b) burst heating, first-order
tau_s = T.tau.to(second).magnitude
t_inf = T.t_inf.to(ureg.degC).magnitude
t = np.linspace(0, 100, 400)
for T0, t_hit, lab, xy in [(T.t_amb, T.t_cold, "from ambient", (3, 30)), (T.t_equil, T.t_hot, "from $S_1$ equilibrium", (12, 92))]:
    T0c = T0.to(ureg.degC).magnitude
    curve = t_inf - (t_inf - T0c) * np.exp(-t / tau_s)
    bx.plot(t, curve, color=R["measured"], lw=1.8, ls="-" if xy[0] < 10 else (0, (5, 2)))
    th = t_hit.to(second).magnitude
    bx.plot(th, T.t_limit.to(ureg.degC).magnitude, "o", color=R["consequence"], ms=5, zorder=5)
    bx.text(th + 2, T.t_limit.to(ureg.degC).magnitude - 4, f"{th:.1f} s", fontsize=8.5, color=R["consequence"], va="top", ha="left")
    bx.text(xy[0], xy[1], lab, fontsize=8.5, color=R["measured"], va="center")
tl = T.t_limit.to(ureg.degC).magnitude
tc = T.t_ceiling.to(ureg.degC).magnitude
bx.axhline(tl, color=R["consequence"], lw=1.2)
bx.text(1, tl + 3, f"insulation class {tl:.0f} °C", ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=R["consequence"])
bx.axhline(tc, color=R["neutral"], lw=0.9, ls="--")
bx.text(99, tc - 3, f"ceiling {tc:.0f} °C", ha="right", va="top", fontsize=8.5, color=R["neutral"])
bx.set_xlim(0, 100)
bx.set_ylim(20, 185)
bx.set_xlabel("Time into the burst (s)")
bx.set_ylabel("Winding temperature (°C)")
bx.text(0.0, 1.03, "(b)", transform=bx.transAxes, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", ha="left", va="bottom")
plt.show()
```
:::

The continuous-duty region ($S_1$) permits sustained operation under the declared cooling conditions. The larger intermittent region ($S_3$) permits periodic bursts only with the starting temperature, duration, and recovery interval established above. Both regions narrow when speed consumes the drive's voltage headroom. Their intersection with the current thermal state, rather than the catalog peak, gives the available torque for the next maneuver.

A simulator that uses only a fixed torque clamp can therefore teach a policy an unavailable action: maximum torque while the rotor is already near its voltage-limited speed, or a repeated burst without recovery. The actuator model and permission limits must include speed and thermal history. Temperature-dependent winding resistance further shrinks the available region during a sustained hold.

The standard remedy in legged-robot sim-to-real transfer replaces the clamp with an actuator model identified on the hardware. For the series elastic actuators of the ANYmal quadruped, @hwangbo2019learning trained a small network on a few minutes of logged joint data to map a short history of position errors and velocities to the torque the actuator actually delivered, then ran it inside the simulator in place of an ideal actuator; the ideal model, which assumes any commanded torque appears instantly, failed to predict the measured torque. The same structure carries the envelope of this section into training: an actuator model that also takes speed, bus voltage, and winding temperature as inputs lets the simulator deny the torque the hardware cannot deliver. @Sec-training-learning-by-trial develops how such models enter the training loop.

### Copper resistance feedback and stall thermal runaway {#sec-body-copper-resistance-feedback}

The copper-resistance rise calculated in @sec-body-thermal-capacity must enter the runtime estimate as well as the design calculation. An external thermistor can lag the winding hotspot, so a thermal observer combines measured current with the characterized heating and cooling model. A discrete update of the lumped energy balance is:
$$\hat{T}_{k+1} = \hat{T}_k + \frac{\Delta t}{C_{\text{th}}} \left[ I_k^2 R(\hat{T}_k) - \frac{\hat{T}_k - T_{\text{amb}}}{\theta_{JA}} \right]$$
where $R(\hat{T}_k) = R_0 [1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}}(\hat{T}_k - T_0)]$. The update interval, model error, and temperature uncertainty must fit the thermal margin. As the estimate approaches its ceiling, the permission path reduces admissible effort or transfers the load to a qualified support mechanism. Removing holding current without securing a gravity-loaded arm would exchange a thermal fault for uncontrolled motion. A static hold shows how copper's feedback changes the sustainable torque (\ref{nbk-body-thermal-stall-derating}).

```{python}
#| label: body-thermal-stall-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ STALL RUNAWAY AND THERMAL DERATING (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: \ref{nbk-body-thermal-stall-derating} in @sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles.
# │ Goal:    Find where the Panda-class elbow's winding settles if it holds the
# │          arm's 87 N m maximum joint torque at stall once copper's
# │          resistance rises with temperature, and the hold it can sustain.
# │ Show:    2.05 N m motor torque, 10.95 A, 59.3 W cold; steady rise 198.4 K
# │          (238.4 C); sustainable 63.89 W at 0.758 Ohm hot, 9.18 A, 73.0 N m
# │          (16.1 percent derating).
# │ How:     Steady state dT = I^2 R0 [1 + alpha (T_amb - T0 + dT)] theta solved
# │          for dT; derating from P_max = (T_limit - T_amb)/theta at R(T_limit).
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import math
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import (
    fmt,
    fmt_int,
    fmt_torque,
    fmt_torque_constant,
    fmt_current,
    fmt_resistance,
    fmt_thermal_resistance,
    fmt_power,
    fmt_temperature,
    fmt_percent,
    check,
)

K = ureg.kelvin

class StallDerating:
    """Steady stall temperature under copper's resistance feedback, and the sustainable hold."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    joint = Actuators.PandaClassJoint.CSG_25_50_ILM70x18  # category: sourced (CSG-25-50 gear with TQ ILM 70x18 motor)
    motor = Actuators.FramelessMotor.TQ_ILM70x18  # category: sourced (TQ-RoboDrive data sheet)
    tau_hold = Embodied.Manipulator.Panda.max_torque  # category: sourced (Panda axes 1-4 maximum joint torque, held statically)
    k_t = motor.torque_constant  # category: sourced (torque per amplitude-invariant i_q, i_d=0)
    r_0 = joint.internal_resistance  # category: sourced (0.75 R_TT at T_0 = 20 C, not per-phase resistance)
    t_0 = ureg.Quantity(20.0, ureg.degC).to(K)  # category: illustrative (resistance reference)
    theta_ja = 1.80 * K / ureg.watt  # category: illustrative (unventilated limb)
    t_amb = ureg.Quantity(40.0, ureg.degC).to(K)  # category: illustrative (limb ambient)
    t_limit = ureg.Quantity(155.0, ureg.degC).to(K)  # category: sourced (IEC 60085 Class F hotspot)
    n_gear = joint.gear_ratio  # category: sourced (CSG-25-50 strain-wave reduction)
    eta = GearRatioCost.eta  # category: illustrative (gear efficiency, declared once in GearRatioCost)
    alpha_cu = 0.00393 / K  # category: sourced (annealed copper, 100 percent IACS, at 20 C; NBS Handbook 100, Copper Wire Tables)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    tau_motor = (tau_hold / (eta * n_gear)).to(ureg.newton * meter)
    i_stall = (tau_motor / k_t).to(ureg.ampere)
    p_cold = (i_stall**2 * r_0).to(ureg.watt)
    gain = (i_stall**2 * r_0 * theta_ja).to(K)  # rise per unit of resistance factor
    const = (gain * (1 + alpha_cu * (t_amb - t_0))).to(K)
    slope = (gain * alpha_cu).to("dimensionless").magnitude
    dt_ss = (const / (1 - slope)).to(K)
    t_wind = (t_amb + dt_ss).to(K)
    p_max = ((t_limit - t_amb) / theta_ja).to(ureg.watt)
    r_hot = (r_0 * (1 + alpha_cu * (t_limit - t_0))).to(ureg.ohm)
    i_max = ((p_max / r_hot) ** 0.5).to(ureg.ampere)
    tau_hold_max = (eta * n_gear * k_t * i_max).to(ureg.newton * meter)
    derate = (1 - tau_hold_max / tau_hold).to("dimensionless").magnitude

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(tau_motor.magnitude - 2.0471) < 1e-4 and abs(i_stall.magnitude - 10.947) < 1e-3, "Unexpected stall current.")
    check(tau_motor < motor.peak_torque, "The stall torque must stay within the motor's peak torque.")
    check(abs(p_cold.magnitude - 59.32) < 0.01, f"Unexpected cold dissipation: {p_cold}")
    check(abs(const.magnitude - 115.16) < 0.01 and abs(slope - 0.4196) < 1e-4, "Unexpected feedback terms.")
    check(abs(dt_ss.magnitude - 198.4) < 0.1, f"Steady rise must be 198.4 K: {dt_ss}")
    check(t_wind > t_limit, "The uncontrolled stall must exceed the insulation limit.")
    check(abs(p_max.magnitude - 63.89) < 0.01, f"Unexpected sustainable dissipation: {p_max}")
    check(abs(i_max.magnitude - 9.18) < 0.01, f"Unexpected sustainable current: {i_max}")
    check(abs(tau_hold_max.magnitude - 73.0) < 0.05, f"Sustainable hold must be 73.0 N m: {tau_hold_max}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    tau_hold_str = fmt_torque(tau_hold, precision=0)
    n_gear_str = fmt_int(n_gear)
    eta_str = fmt(eta, precision=2)
    k_t_str = fmt_torque_constant(k_t, precision=3)
    r_0_str = fmt_resistance(r_0, unit=ureg.ohm, precision=3)
    t_0_str = fmt_temperature(t_0, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    theta_ja_str = fmt_thermal_resistance(theta_ja, precision=2)
    t_amb_str = fmt_temperature(t_amb, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    t_limit_str = fmt_temperature(t_limit, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    tau_motor_str = fmt_torque(tau_motor, precision=2)
    i_stall_str = fmt_current(i_stall, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=1)
    p_cold_str = fmt_power(p_cold, unit=ureg.watt, precision=1)
    const_str = fmt(const.magnitude, precision=2)
    slope_str = fmt(slope, precision=4)
    dt_ss_str = fmt_temperature(dt_ss, unit=ureg.kelvin, precision=1)
    t_wind_str = fmt_temperature(t_wind, unit=ureg.degC, precision=1)
    dt_max_str = fmt_temperature((t_limit - t_amb).to(K), unit=ureg.kelvin, precision=0)
    p_max_str = fmt_power(p_max, unit=ureg.watt, precision=2)
    r_hot_str = fmt_resistance(r_hot, unit=ureg.ohm, precision=3)
    i_max_str = fmt_current(i_max, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=2)
    tau_hold_max_str = fmt_torque(tau_hold_max, precision=1)
    derate_pct_str = fmt_percent(derate, precision=1, style="prose")
```

::: {#nbk-body-thermal-stall-derating .callout-notebook title="Static holding torque and stall derating"}
The arm's elbow, the same Panda-class stand-in joint as \ref{nbk-body-thermal-burst-limits}, is asked to hold the arm's maximum joint torque $\tau_{\text{hold}} =$ `{python} StallDerating.tau_hold_str` at stall ($\omega = 0$) through its $N =$ `{python} StallDerating.n_gear_str`:1 strain-wave gear ($\eta =$ `{python} StallDerating.eta_str`, illustrative). Its motor has $K_t =$ `{python} StallDerating.k_t_str`, cold effective aggregate loss resistance $R_0 =$ `{python} StallDerating.r_0_str` at $T_0 =$ `{python} StallDerating.t_0_str`, and $\theta_{JA} =$ `{python} StallDerating.theta_ja_str`, with a Class F limit of `{python} StallDerating.t_limit_str`, inside an unventilated limb at $T_{\text{amb}} =$ `{python} StallDerating.t_amb_str`.

**Problem**: With copper's resistance rising with temperature, where does the stalled winding settle, and what holding torque is thermally sustainable?

**Math**:

1. **Stall current**: $\tau_{\text{motor}} = \tau_{\text{hold}}/(\eta N) =$ `{python} StallDerating.tau_motor_str`, so $I = \tau_{\text{motor}}/K_t =$ `{python} StallDerating.i_stall_str` and the cold dissipation is $P_0 = I^2 R_0 =$ `{python} StallDerating.p_cold_str`.
2. **Runaway**: With $R(T) = R_0[1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}}(T - T_0)]$, the steady rise satisfies
   $$\Delta T = I^2 R_0 \left[1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}}(T_{\text{amb}} - T_0 + \Delta T)\right] \theta_{JA}$$
   Rearranging terms yields $\Delta T = \frac{I^2 R_0 [1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}}(T_{\text{amb}} - T_0)] \theta_{JA}}{1 - I^2 R_0 \theta_{JA} \alpha_{\text{Cu}}}$. The denominator establishes the **thermal runaway criterion**: if the positive feedback loop gain satisfies $I^2 R_0 \theta_{JA} \alpha_{\text{Cu}} \ge 1$, this fixed-current, linear-resistance model cannot settle to a stable thermal equilibrium. Above one, heat generation increases with temperature faster than heat removal, producing exponential growth; at exactly one, the temperature-dependent terms cancel and the remaining positive heating causes linear growth. In this stall scenario, the feedback factor is `{python} StallDerating.slope_str` $< 1$, so temperature settles at a finite (yet fatal) equilibrium: $\Delta T =$ `{python} StallDerating.const_str` $+$ `{python} StallDerating.slope_str` $\Delta T$, yielding $\Delta T =$ `{python} StallDerating.dt_ss_str` and driving the winding to `{python} StallDerating.t_wind_str`, far above its rating.

3. **Derating**: At the limit the allowable rise is `{python} StallDerating.dt_max_str`, so the sustainable dissipation is $P_{\max} = \Delta T_{\max}/\theta_{JA} =$ `{python} StallDerating.p_max_str`. At the hot resistance $R(T_{\text{limit}}) \approx$ `{python} StallDerating.r_hot_str`, that allows $I_{\max} = \sqrt{P_{\max}/R} \approx$ `{python} StallDerating.i_max_str` and a hold of $\tau_{\text{hold,max}} = \eta N K_t I_{\max} \approx$ `{python} StallDerating.tau_hold_max_str`.

**Result**: Held without control, the stall drives the winding toward `{python} StallDerating.t_wind_str`, and staying within the insulation rating requires a `{python} StallDerating.derate_pct_str` derating, from `{python} StallDerating.tau_hold_str` to `{python} StallDerating.tau_hold_max_str`. Continuous gravity holding above the qualified continuous torque requires another support mechanism, such as a friction brake or counterweight; holding within that torque can remain electrically sustained under the stated thermal conditions.
:::

Delivering the current pulses that generate these thermal loads also stresses the upstream electrical supply, moving the burden from heat in the copper to transient current on the power bus.

## Electrical Power Integrity {#sec-body-power-integrity}

When the mobile manipulator swerves hard to avoid a collision, every drive motor, joint inverter, and accelerator demands peak current at once from one direct-current distribution bus. In simulation, current flows from an idealized source. On hardware, delivery is bounded by finite capacity, source impedance, and transient voltage stability. **A machine that browns out mid-motion fails physically; the electrical supply is a shared resource.**

Rail sag, regenerative overvoltage, and thermal accumulation are manifestations of one bounded energy network on different time scales. Of the three, voltage moves fastest, within microseconds to milliseconds whenever current demand exceeds what the source can deliver at that instant. Compute, sensing, and motor inverters draw from a common bus, so when a policy commands coordinated accelerations across several joints, the sum of their currents changes the voltage delivered to every node on the machine.

### Power distribution impedance, transient droop, and brownout resets {#sec-body-power-distribution-impedance}

The mobile machine's battery, harnesses, connectors, and protection switches all contribute source impedance.[^fn-hw-bus-resistance] Local capacitors supply part of a sudden load increase, so current drawn by the loads need not equal current arriving through the harness. For a source feeding one bus node through resistance and inductance,
$$V_{\text{source}}(t)-V_{\text{bus}}(t)=R_{\text{bus}}I_{\text{source}}(t)+L_{\text{bus}}\frac{dI_{\text{source}}}{dt}$$ {#eq-body-droop}
where $R_{\text{bus}}$ is the lumped source resistance, $L_{\text{bus}}$ is the loop inductance, and $I_{\text{source}}$ is the current through that source path. The local capacitor bank $C_{\text{bus}}$ supplies the difference between load current $I_{\text{load}}$ and source current. In the ideal-capacitor model, charge removed from that bank lowers the same bus voltage:
$$V_{\text{bus}}(0)-V_{\text{bus}}(t)=\frac{1}{C_{\text{bus}}}\int_0^t\left[I_{\text{load}}(s)-I_{\text{source}}(s)\right]ds.$$
These equations jointly determine the voltage response; the capacitor's voltage change is not an additional drop to add to @eq-body-droop. @Sec-appendix-systems-power develops this source-and-capacitor model.

Compute and motion must be budgeted together because they share this path. An obstacle response can require fresh inference at the same time as a large drive-current change. Testing each load separately misses the combined step that the supply must support.

Harness inductance limits how quickly source current can rise. Local capacitors supply the initial current deficit, while harness resistance continues to lower the rail after source current catches up with a sustained load. Once the currents settle, the inductive voltage is zero and the sustained drop is $I_{\text{source}}R_{\text{bus}}$. The worked example below screens that sustained condition; it does not establish the minimum voltage during the transient. If the actual voltage crosses a regulator's undervoltage threshold, computation or communication may stop or reset. Power qualification must establish the voltage at the supplied devices during coincident load and the physical response if those devices lose power.

[^fn-hw-bus-resistance]: **Power distribution bus impedance and capacitor buffering**\index{Bus impedance!power distribution}\index{Brownout reset!undervoltage}: The lumped source resistance is $R_{\text{bus}} = R_{\text{cell}} + R_{\text{harness}} + R_{\text{switch}}$, the sum of battery cell, harness and connector, and protection-switch on-state resistances. Source inductance governs how quickly harness current changes; capacitor discharge bridges the resulting current deficit. Both affect the same bus voltage, so their effects must be solved together rather than added as independent droop estimates. Capacitor series resistance and the actual source response also matter during a transient. The sustained ohmic screen below is therefore the first check on the rail, not the last.

That reset turns the electrical fault into a mechanical one. Voltage supervisors pull the reset line on microcontrollers and gate drivers, clocks halt, register configurations vanish, and communication buses float. An acceleration command issued just before the reset stays physically active until the gate-driver stage collapses. If the driver then floats, phase current ceases, torque falls to zero, and the body coasts under gravity and inertia into workpieces or hardstops. If it instead shorts the low-side switches for dynamic braking, back-EMF ($e_{\text{bemf}} = K_e \omega$) produces an immediate, violent counter-torque that jerks the mechanics at the joint limits.

```{python}
#| label: body-spring-brake-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ SPRING-BRAKE ENGAGEMENT ON THE RUNNING MACHINE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the unpowered-states paragraph in @sec-body-power-integrity.
# │ Goal:    Give the interval after coil decay during which a spring-applied
# │          brake on any of the machine's nine axes has not yet engaged.
# │ Show:    30 ms to 80 ms.
# │ How:     RM.spring_brake_engage_min and RM.spring_brake_engage_max.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_latency, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator

class SpringBrake:
    """Spring-brake engagement window after coil decay."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    t_engage_min = RM.spring_brake_engage_min  # category: illustrative (fast end)
    t_engage_max = RM.spring_brake_engage_max  # category: illustrative (slow end)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    t_window = (t_engage_max - t_engage_min).to(millisecond)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(t_engage_min.to(millisecond).magnitude - 30.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected fast engage: {t_engage_min}")
    check(abs(t_engage_max.to(millisecond).magnitude - 80.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected slow engage: {t_engage_max}")
    check(t_window.magnitude > 0, "The slow end must follow the fast end.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    t_engage_min_str = fmt_latency(t_engage_min, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_engage_max_str = fmt_latency(t_engage_max, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
```

### Unpowered states and unmanaged fallback dynamics {#sec-body-unpowered-states}

```{python}
#| label: body-phase-short-peak-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ WHERE PHASE-SHORT BRAKING PEAKS ON THE HUB MOTORS (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the unpowered-states paragraph in @sec-body-unpowered-states.
# │ Goal:    Locate the speed at which short-circuit braking torque peaks on
# │          the running machine's hub motors and compare it with the drive
# │          limit.
# │ Show:    omega_e = R/L = 371 rad/s; with 20 pole pairs the wheel speed is
# │          18.6 rad/s, about 177 rpm, above the 108 rpm of the 1.5 m/s drive
# │          limit.
# │ How:     tau_short = K^2 omega R / (R^2 + (P_n omega L)^2) peaks at
# │          P_n omega L = R; line R and L (same ratio as per phase).
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_angular_velocity, check

class PhaseShortPeak:
    """Speed of peak short-circuit braking torque for the hub motors."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    hub = BrakingLimits.hub  # category: sourced (ZLTECH ZLLG10ASM800 datasheet)
    omega_drive = BrakingLimits.omega  # category: derived (wheel speed at the drive limit)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    omega_e_peak = (hub.line_resistance / hub.line_inductance).to(ureg.radian / second)
    omega_m_peak = (omega_e_peak / hub.pole_pairs).to(ureg.rpm)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(omega_e_peak.magnitude - 371.35) < 0.01, f"Unexpected electrical peak speed: {omega_e_peak}")
    check(abs(omega_m_peak.magnitude - 177.31) < 0.01, f"Unexpected wheel speed at the peak: {omega_m_peak}")
    check(omega_m_peak > omega_drive, "The peak must lie above the drive-limit wheel speed.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    omega_m_peak_str = fmt_angular_velocity(omega_m_peak, unit=ureg.rpm, precision=1)
    omega_drive_str = fmt_angular_velocity(omega_drive, unit=ureg.rpm, precision=1)
```

Power removal is an unmanaged state transition, not an automatic return to safety. Cutting power leaves an actuator in one of three unpowered states, namely free coasting, phase-short dynamic braking, or spring-engaged mechanical braking, and each enforces a distinct mechanical behavior. Free coasting simply allows gravity to accelerate unconstrained joints without any resistance. An electromechanical friction brake requires `{python} SpringBrake.t_engage_min_str` to `{python} SpringBrake.t_engage_max_str` for its mechanical spring to overcome magnetic coil decay and engage its friction pads, during which gravity accelerates an overhead arm downward.

Phase-short dynamic braking generates a counter-torque that at low speed grows in proportion to angular velocity ($\tau \approx \frac{K_t K_e}{R_{\text{phase}}} \omega$) and gives zero holding torque at zero velocity. The proportionality does not last. As speed rises, the winding inductance limits the short-circuit current. The shorted winding is a resistance and an inductance driven by the back-EMF $K_e\omega$, which alternates at the electrical speed $P_n\omega$. An inductance opposes an alternating current in proportion to its frequency, with reactance $P_n\omega L$, and that opposition adds to the resistance in quadrature, so the current is $K_e\omega/\sqrt{R^2 + (P_n\omega L)^2}$, and the braking torque, the power dissipated in $R$ divided by $\omega$, is $K_t K_e \omega R/(R^2 + (P_n\omega L)^2)$. That torque peaks where the electrical speed $P_n \omega$ equals $R/L$ and falls beyond it, so above that speed a phase short brakes less the faster the joint turns. For the base's hub motors that peak lies at `{python} PhaseShortPeak.omega_m_peak_str` of the wheel, above the `{python} PhaseShortPeak.omega_drive_str` of the drive limit, so the proportional picture holds across the base's speed range; a fast, high-ratio joint motor has no such guarantee.

Industrial standards name these responses. IEC 60204-1 defines stop category 0 as immediate removal of power from the machine actuators, category 1 as a controlled stop with power kept available until the machine has stopped and then removed, and category 2 as a controlled stop that leaves power available [@iec60204]. The drive safety functions of IEC 61800-5-2 implement them: Safe Torque Off (STO) removes the torque-producing drive signals and leaves the joint in free coast, Safe Stop 1 (SS1) decelerates the motor and then applies STO, and Safe Brake Control (SBC) switches the spring brake [@iec61800part52]; @sec-nervous-actuation-authority places STO in the machine's interlock. The trajectory a machine follows after an electrical cutoff must be measured under full mechanical payload, not deduced from circuit diagrams. The choice of which safe fallback state the machine should enter belongs to system safety architecture in @sec-enforcement, but the physical dynamics of an unpowered joint are unalterable mechanical constraints of the body.

### Regenerative overvoltage surges and dynamic brake choppers {#sec-body-regenerative-surges}

Regenerative deceleration drives the bus toward its opposite boundary, overvoltage, as part of the machine's kinetic energy returns electrically. **Returned braking energy needs an absorption or dissipation path.** A battery cannot be assumed to accept it under every state of charge, temperature, or protection state. If the battery management system disconnects charge input, the remaining bus components must handle the regenerated energy without exceeding their voltage ratings.

Under the conservative assumption that the battery management system has disconnected and the local bus capacitance $C_{\text{bus}}$ must absorb the entire returned kinetic energy $E_{\text{regen}}$ without dissipation, the terminal DC bus voltage rises to:
$$V_{\text{final}} = \sqrt{V_{\text{initial}}^2 + \frac{2 E_{\text{regen}}}{C_{\text{bus}}}}$$
where $V_{\text{initial}}$ is the bus voltage when deceleration begins (@sec-appendix-systems derives this energy balance). The worst case is a full pack, the state in which the battery management system refuses further charge.

The capacitor-only endpoint is a screening calculation: if it exceeds a component rating, the stop requires another energy path. A dynamic brake chopper switches an absorption resistor across the bus when voltage reaches a chosen clamp threshold.[^fn-hw-brake-chopper] Its resistor must handle both the peak regenerated power and the pulse energy, with enough recovery between stops. The worked bus calculation below sizes the peak-power requirement for the warehouse machine.

[^fn-hw-brake-chopper]: **Dynamic Braking Chopper Circuit**\index{Dynamic brake chopper!regenerative clamp}\index{Overvoltage protection!dynamic braking}: A power switch and a low-inductance braking resistor placed across the DC bus. When regenerated energy drives the bus above a comparator threshold, the switch conducts and the resistor dissipates the excess as heat, clamping the bus below the breakdown rating of the inverter and converter silicon.

Power integrity is an architectural constraint. The design sets coordinated power budgets and current slew-rate limits across accelerators and drives, the permission path arbitrates simultaneous multi-axis accelerations so that their $dI/dt$ transients do not compound, and brake choppers protect the inverters from regenerative feedback during emergency stops. \ref{nbk-body-dc-bus-power-integrity} works both halves of that budget, the bus's sag and the stop's regenerative surge, on the mobile manipulator's 48 V drive bus.

```{python}
#| label: body-dc-bus-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ 48 V DRIVE-BUS DROOP AND REGENERATIVE SURGE ON THE RUNNING MACHINE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: \ref{nbk-body-dc-bus-power-integrity} in @sec-body-power-integrity,
# │          the ranking of margins in @sec-body-archetype-matrix, and the rail
# │          column of @tbl-02-limit-record.
# │ Goal:    Screen sustained coincident load on the 48 V drive bus against the
# │          48-to-24 V converter's undervoltage lockout, and regenerative
# │          voltage during a stop from the drive limit; the transient minimum
# │          requires separate qualification.
# │ Show:    70 A through 60 mOhm drops 4.2 V: 54 -> 49.8 V full, 42 -> 37.8 V
# │          depleted, 4.8 V above the 33 V lockout (150 A would cross it);
# │          75 percent of 414 J = 310.5 J; capacitor-only endpoint from 54 V
# │          about 176.5 V; 750 ms stop, 828 W peak; chopper resistor
# │          <= 4.35 Ohm at the 60 V clamp; 100 V switches.
# │ How:     calc_voltage_droop with RM.drive_bus_* and AISLE.i_rail_transient;
# │          compute share from the Orin TDP through the converter efficiency;
# │          E_k from MachineMomentum.e_k; capacitor energy balance from full
# │          charge; triangular power pulse over t_stop = v / a_brake.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import (
    fmt_mass,
    fmt_capacitance,
    fmt_voltage,
    fmt_current,
    fmt_resistance,
    fmt_power,
    fmt_energy,
    fmt_latency,
    fmt_velocity,
    fmt_acceleration,
    fmt_percent,
    fmt_display_math,
    check,
)

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class DriveBusIntegrity:
    """48 V drive-bus droop, regenerative surge, and chopper sizing for the running machine."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    m = RM.loaded_mass  # category: derived (upper bound, full tote rack)
    v = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
    a_brake = AISLE.a_brake  # category: illustrative (credible deceleration)
    e_k = MachineMomentum.e_k  # category: derived (loaded machine at its drive limit)
    v_full = RM.drive_bus_full_charge  # category: sourced (48 V-class pack maximum)
    v_bus_nom = RM.drive_bus_nominal  # category: sourced (48 V-class pack nominal)
    v_battery_low = RM.drive_bus_battery_low  # category: sourced (48 V-class pack minimum)
    r_bus = RM.drive_bus_resistance  # category: illustrative (source path; needs a measured value)
    v_uvlo = RM.drive_bus_uvlo  # category: sourced (48-to-24 V converter input lockout)
    v_conv_max = RM.drive_bus_converter_max  # category: sourced (converter continuous input maximum)
    eff_conv = RM.drive_bus_converter_efficiency  # category: sourced (converter typical efficiency)
    p_soc = RM.brain_soc.tdp  # category: sourced (application processor TDP)
    di = AISLE.i_rail_transient  # category: illustrative (inference burst plus drive)
    c_bus = 22000.0 * ureg.microfarad  # category: illustrative (bulk link capacitance)
    v_breakdown = RM.drive_bus_switch_rating  # category: chosen (100 V switch class)
    v_clamp = RM.drive_bus_clamp  # category: chosen (chopper clamp threshold)
    regen_fraction = 0.75  # category: illustrative (share of E_k returned to the bus)
    r_candidate = 3.9 * ureg.ohm  # category: chosen (candidate chopper resistor)
    p_candidate = 1.0 * ureg.kilowatt  # category: chosen (candidate resistor pulse rating)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    i_compute = (p_soc / (eff_conv * v_bus_nom)).to(ureg.ampere)
    i_drive = (di - i_compute).to(ureg.ampere)
    dv = calc_voltage_droop(di, r_bus).to(volt)  # sustained resistive drop, not a transient minimum
    v_sustained = (v_full - dv).to(volt)
    v_sag_low = (v_battery_low - dv).to(volt)
    margin_low = (v_sag_low - v_uvlo).to(volt)
    headroom_low = (v_battery_low - v_uvlo).to(volt)
    i_cross = ((v_battery_low - v_uvlo) / r_bus).to(ureg.ampere)

    e_regen = (regen_fraction * e_k).to(joule)
    v_final = ((v_full**2 + 2 * e_regen / c_bus) ** 0.5).to(volt)
    e_cap_to_clamp = (0.5 * c_bus * (v_clamp**2 - v_full**2)).to(joule)
    t_stop = (v / a_brake).to(millisecond)
    p_peak = (2 * e_regen / t_stop).to(ureg.watt)
    r_max = (v_clamp**2 / p_peak).to(ureg.ohm)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(dv.magnitude - 4.2) < 1e-9, f"Resistive drop must be 4.2 V: {dv}")
    check(abs(v_sustained.magnitude - 49.8) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected full-charge sustained voltage: {v_sustained}")
    check(abs(v_sag_low.magnitude - 37.8) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected depleted sustained voltage: {v_sag_low}")
    check(abs(margin_low.magnitude - 4.8) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected depleted margin: {margin_low}")
    check(v_sag_low > v_uvlo, "At 48 V the sustained screen must stay above the converter lockout even when depleted.")
    check(abs(i_cross.magnitude - 150.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected crossing current: {i_cross}")
    check(i_compute < di, "The compute share must be part of the coincident step.")
    check(abs(e_k.magnitude - 414.0) < 1e-6, f"Unexpected kinetic energy: {e_k}")
    check(abs(e_regen.magnitude - 310.5) < 1e-6, f"Unexpected regenerated energy: {e_regen}")
    check(abs(v_final.magnitude - 176.47) < 0.01, f"Unexpected capacitor-only endpoint: {v_final}")
    check(e_cap_to_clamp < e_regen, "The capacitor alone must not absorb the stop before the clamp.")
    check(abs(t_stop.magnitude - 750.0) < 1e-6, f"Unexpected stop duration: {t_stop}")
    check(abs(p_peak.magnitude - 828.0) < 1e-6, f"Unexpected regenerative peak: {p_peak}")
    check(
        abs(p_peak.magnitude - (regen_fraction * m * a_brake * v).to(ureg.watt).magnitude) < 1e-6,
        "The triangular-pulse peak must equal the regenerated share of m*a*v.",
    )
    check(abs(r_max.magnitude - 4.3478) < 1e-3, f"Unexpected chopper resistance bound: {r_max}")
    check(r_candidate <= r_max and p_candidate >= p_peak, "The candidate resistor must meet both bounds.")
    check(v_full < v_clamp <= v_conv_max < v_breakdown, "Clamp above full charge, within the converter, below the switches.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    m_str = fmt_mass(m, unit=kilogram, precision=0)
    v_str = fmt_velocity(v, unit=meter / second, precision=1)
    a_brake_str = fmt_acceleration(a_brake, unit=meter / second**2, precision=0)
    v_full_str = fmt_voltage(v_full, unit=volt, precision=0)
    v_bus_nom_str = fmt_voltage(v_bus_nom, unit=volt, precision=1)
    v_battery_low_str = fmt_voltage(v_battery_low, unit=volt, precision=0)
    r_bus_str = fmt_resistance(r_bus, unit=ureg.milliohm, precision=0)
    c_bus_str = fmt_capacitance(c_bus, unit=ureg.microfarad, precision=0, commas=True)
    v_uvlo_str = fmt_voltage(v_uvlo, unit=volt, precision=0)
    v_conv_max_str = fmt_voltage(v_conv_max, unit=volt, precision=1)
    v_breakdown_str = fmt_voltage(v_breakdown, unit=volt, precision=0)
    p_soc_str = fmt_power(p_soc, unit=ureg.watt, precision=0)
    eff_conv_pct_str = fmt_percent(eff_conv, precision=0, style="prose")
    i_drive_str = fmt_current(i_drive, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=1)
    i_compute_str = fmt_current(i_compute, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=1)
    di_str = fmt_current(di, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=0)
    dv_str = fmt_voltage(dv, unit=volt, precision=1)
    v_sustained_str = fmt_voltage(v_sustained, unit=volt, precision=1)
    v_sag_low_str = fmt_voltage(v_sag_low, unit=volt, precision=1)
    margin_low_str = fmt_voltage(margin_low, unit=volt, precision=1)
    headroom_low_str = fmt_voltage(headroom_low, unit=volt, precision=0)
    i_cross_str = fmt_current(i_cross, unit=ureg.ampere, precision=0)
    dv_display_math = fmt_display_math(rf"\Delta V_{{\text{{sustained}}}} = \Delta I R_{{\text{{bus}}}} = {dv_str}")
    v_sag_display_math = fmt_display_math(
        rf"V_{{\text{{bus, sustained}}}} = {v_full_str} - {dv_str} = {v_sustained_str} \text{{ (full)}}, \quad {v_battery_low_str} - {dv_str} = {v_sag_low_str} \text{{ (depleted)}}"
    )
    e_k_display_math = fmt_display_math(
        rf"E_k = \tfrac{{1}}{{2}} m v^2 = \tfrac{{1}}{{2}}\,({m_str})({v_str})^2 = {fmt_energy(e_k, unit=joule, precision=0)}"
    )
    regen_pct_str = fmt_percent(regen_fraction, precision=0, style="prose")
    e_regen_str = fmt_energy(e_regen, unit=joule, precision=1)
    v_final_display_math = fmt_display_math(
        rf"V_{{\text{{final}}}} = \sqrt{{V_{{\text{{full}}}}^2 + \frac{{2 E_{{\text{{regen}}}}}}{{C_{{\text{{bus}}}}}}}} \approx {fmt_voltage(v_final, unit=volt, precision=1)}"
    )
    e_cap_to_clamp_str = fmt_energy(e_cap_to_clamp, unit=joule, precision=1)
    t_stop_str = fmt_latency(t_stop, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    v_clamp_str = fmt_voltage(v_clamp, unit=volt, precision=0)
    p_peak_display_math = fmt_display_math(
        rf"P_{{\text{{regen, peak}}}} \approx \frac{{2 E_{{\text{{regen}}}}}}{{t_{{\text{{stop}}}}}} = {fmt_power(p_peak, unit=ureg.watt, precision=0)}"
    )
    r_max_display_math = fmt_display_math(
        rf"R_{{\text{{brake}}}} \le \frac{{V_{{\text{{clamp}}}}^2}}{{P_{{\text{{regen, peak}}}}}} \approx {fmt_resistance(r_max, unit=ureg.ohm, precision=2)}"
    )
    r_max_str = fmt_resistance(r_max, unit=ureg.ohm, precision=2)
    r_candidate_str = fmt_resistance(r_candidate, unit=ureg.ohm, precision=1)
    p_candidate_str = fmt_power(p_candidate, unit=ureg.kilowatt, precision=0)
    p_peak_str = fmt_power(p_peak, unit=ureg.watt, precision=0)
```

::: {#nbk-body-dc-bus-power-integrity .callout-notebook title="DC bus voltage sag and regenerative surge"}
The mobile manipulator's lithium-ion pack feeds a `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_bus_nom_str` nominal drive bus, with the voltage envelope of a commercial 48 V-class mobile robot's pack [@mir2025mir250]. The bus carries the wheel drives, the arm's joint drives, and a 48-to-24 V converter that supplies the application processor and control electronics. The converter shuts off when its input falls to `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_uvlo_str` [@meanwell2026ddr240].

**Problem**: Under the coincident current step of an inference burst and the drive motors, and then a stop from the drive limit, does the bus remain within the operating limits of the converter and the motor inverters?

**Math**:

1. **Parameters**:
   - Machine mass, travel speed, and credible deceleration: $m =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.m_str` (upper bound, full tote rack), $v =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_str`, $a_{\text{brake}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.a_brake_str`
   - Bus characteristics: pack voltage from `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_full_str` at full charge to `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_battery_low_str` depleted, source resistance $R_{\text{bus}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.r_bus_str` (illustrative), bulk link capacitance $C_{\text{bus}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.c_bus_str`
   - Operating limits: converter lockout $V_{\text{uvlo}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_uvlo_str`, converter continuous input maximum `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_conv_max_str`, inverter switch rating $V_{\text{breakdown}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_breakdown_str`
2. **Sustained-load screen**:
   - As an illustrative coincident load, the two drive motors and the arm's joint drives add `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.i_drive_str` while the application processor, drawing its `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.p_soc_str` thermal design power (TDP) through the converter at `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.eff_conv_pct_str` efficiency, adds `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.i_compute_str`. Their aggregate increase is $\Delta I =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.di_str`. Assume the stated pack voltage is the unloaded source voltage and this coincident demand is the total load in the screen.
   - After source current settles to the increased load, the additional resistive drop is:
     `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.dv_display_math`
   - The resulting sustained bus voltage at full charge and when depleted is:
     `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_sag_display_math`
   - Even from the depleted pack, the bus stays `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.margin_low_str` above the converter's lockout; it would take a `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.i_cross_str` step to spend the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.headroom_low_str` between the depleted pack and the lockout. This screen does not establish the transient minimum, which inductance and capacitor depletion push lower.
3. **Regenerative surge**:
   - During a stop from the drive limit, the loaded machine's kinetic energy must be dissipated:
     `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.e_k_display_math`
   - A full pack is the worst case, because that is when the battery management system refuses charge. If it disconnects charge input and an illustrative `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.regen_pct_str` of kinetic energy returns to the bus ($E_{\text{regen}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.e_regen_str`), an unprotected, lossless capacitor-only energy balance would end at:
     `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_final_display_math`
   - *Failure mechanism*: Raising the capacitor from full charge to the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_clamp_str` clamp absorbs only `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.e_cap_to_clamp_str` of the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.e_regen_str`, so long before the bus reached that endpoint it would cross the converter's input maximum and then the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_breakdown_str` switch rating.
4. **Dynamic braking clamp**:
   - Under deceleration over $t_{\text{stop}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.t_stop_str`, regenerative power peaks at `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.p_peak_display_math`
   - The clamp $V_{\text{clamp}} =$ `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_clamp_str` sits above the full-charge voltage, so it never fires while charging, and within the converter's input range. To hold it there, the brake chopper must divert this peak power through an absorption resistor:
     `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.r_max_display_math`

**Result**: The sustained-load screen leaves the bus at `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_sustained_str` from a full pack and `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_sag_low_str` from a depleted one, `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.margin_low_str` above the converter lockout. Unbuffered regenerative braking would drive the bus past the converter's input maximum and the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_breakdown_str` switch rating, which calls for a dynamic brake chopper whose resistor is no larger than `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.r_max_str` and absorbs an `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.p_peak_str` peak (satisfied by an illustrative `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.r_candidate_str`, `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.p_candidate_str` component).

**Systems insight**: Mechanical motion and electrical power are bidirectionally coupled. Acceleration requires a supply that sustains the coincident current demand; deceleration requires an adequate absorption or dissipation path. On this 48 V bus the depleted pack still sits `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.headroom_low_str` above the converter lockout, more than twice this step's resistive drop, so the sustained screen passes; the transient minimum, pulse energy, repetition, cooling, and component tolerances still require qualification.
:::

```{python}
#| label: body-conveyor-freshness-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ FRESHNESS DEADLINE FOR THE MUG ON THE CONVEYOR (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the freshness item of \ref{chk-body-bus-droop-regen}.
# │ Goal:    Give the moving target the freshness deadline applies to on the
# │          running machine: the mug on the pick-station conveyor.
# │ Show:    0.20 m/s, 15 mm grasp tolerance, 3 mm of it spent by the initial
# │          estimate; the answer (not printed) is (15 - 3) / 0.20 = 60 ms.
# │ How:     Delta t_fresh = e_max / v_max with e_max = r_tol - e_0, from AISLE.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_length, fmt_velocity, check

AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class ConveyorFreshness:
    """Freshness deadline for the mug riding the pick-station conveyor."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    v_conv = AISLE.v_conveyor  # category: illustrative (conveyor speed)
    r_tol = AISLE.grasp_tolerance  # category: chosen (grasp tolerance)
    e_0 = AISLE.grasp_initial_error  # category: illustrative (initial estimate error)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    dt_fresh = ((r_tol - e_0) / v_conv).to(millisecond)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(v_conv.to(meter / second).magnitude - 0.20) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected conveyor speed: {v_conv}")
    check(abs(r_tol.to(ureg.millimeter).magnitude - 15.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected grasp tolerance: {r_tol}")
    check(abs(e_0.to(ureg.millimeter).magnitude - 3.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected initial error: {e_0}")
    check(abs(dt_fresh.magnitude - 60.0) < 1e-9, f"Conveyor freshness deadline must be 60 ms: {dt_fresh}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    v_conv_str = fmt_velocity(v_conv, unit=meter / second, precision=2)
    r_tol_str = fmt_length(r_tol, unit=ureg.millimeter, precision=0)
    e_0_str = fmt_length(e_0, unit=ureg.millimeter, precision=0)
```

::: {#chk-body-bus-droop-regen .callout-checkpoint title="The five physical budgets"}

Before measuring these limits on an assembled machine, verify your understanding of the five budgets:

- [ ] **Freshness deadline**: Can you calculate the maximum allowable measurement age for the mug riding the pick-station conveyor at `{python} ConveyorFreshness.v_conv_str`, with a `{python} ConveyorFreshness.r_tol_str` grasp tolerance of which the initial estimate already spends `{python} ConveyorFreshness.e_0_str`, and explain why that age is counted from exposure on the sensor rather than from the start of inference, and why the base's stop for a standing person instead charges age as blind travel?
- [ ] **Velocity ceiling**: Can you explain why doubling the pre-brake delay expands the stopping distance linearly while doubling travel speed expands the braking term quadratically, and why the admissible speed is the positive root of $d_{\text{stop}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$?
- [ ] **Inertia matching**: Can you explain why the gear ratio that maximizes link acceleration makes reflected rotor inertia equal load inertia ($N^2 J_{\text{rotor}} = J_{\text{load}}$), and why oversizing the gearbox for static torque lowers dynamic joint acceleration?
- [ ] **Thermal horizons and runaway**: Can you explain why an actuator can produce three times its rated torque for seconds but overheats its winding insulation if held there for minutes, and how the temperature coefficient of copper ($\alpha_{\text{Cu}}$) turns a sustained stall into runaway?
- [ ] **Rail sag and regeneration**: Can you explain how a coincident compute and drive current step sags a shared rail through resistance, inductance, and capacitor depletion, and why a stop from speed pumps energy back into the bus that a brake chopper must divert?

:::

## Measuring a Machine's Own Limits {#sec-body-measuring-limits}

A brake that stops an unloaded base on a cool laboratory floor has not established how the loaded mobile manipulator stops after repeated maneuvers. Characterization must connect each calculation to measurements under the conditions in which the machine will use it. A dynamometer, a test stand that applies a controlled mechanical load, isolates actuator behavior; a propulsion stand does the same with a propeller as the load (@fig-02-real-motor-dyno-bench). Integrated trials then establish what changes when the actuator shares a chassis, cooling path, and power supply with the rest of the machine. A defensible limit states what was measured, how uncertain the result is, and which conditions must remain true for a later decision to rely on it.

### Empirical dynamometer characterization and probe intrusion {#sec-body-dynamometer-characterization}

On a dynamometer, a controlled load machine resists the actuator while torque, speed, current, and voltage are measured on a shared timebase. Four tests connect the earlier models to measurable parameters:

- **Torque and back-EMF transduction ($K_t$ and $K_e$)**: By commanding the inverter's Field-Oriented Control (FOC) current loop across a sweep of quadrature phase currents $i_q$ while the dynamometer absorbs torque at constant speed, engineers measure electromechanical torque transduction:
  $$\tau = K_t i_q$$
  Driving the unpowered motor at known speed and measuring open-circuit voltage supplies the corresponding back-EMF constant $K_e = e_{\text{bemf}} / \omega$. These tests establish the conversion factors used in @sec-body-electrical-time-constants.

- **Electrical rise time and inductive bandwidth ($\tau_e = L/R$)**: With the rotor held so that the test current produces no torque, the inverter applies a small voltage step $V_{\text{step}}$ across the winding. The current response:
  $$i(t) = \frac{V_{\text{step}}}{R}\left(1 - e^{-t/\tau_e}\right)$$
  reveals the electrical time constant. The step must stay small, because its steady current $V_{\text{step}}/R$ flows through a winding of low resistance: the full `{python} CurrentRise.v_low_str` of a depleted pack across a hub motor's `{python} CurrentRise.r_line_str` would drive `{python} CurrentRise.i_full_step_str`, `{python} CurrentRise.step_over_peak_mult_str` the motor's peak current. The current probe and acquisition path must resolve the rise; otherwise the instrument smooths the response being measured and hides the actuator limit.

- **Enclosed thermal resistance ($\theta_{JA}$) and continuous torque ceilings**: A heating trial under the installed cooling conditions measures the winding temperature rise and loss power, establishing $\theta_{JA} = \Delta T / P_{\text{loss}}$. The continuous torque ceiling from @sec-body-thermal-capacity is then:
  $$\tau_{\text{cont}} = K_t \sqrt{\frac{T_{\max} - T_{\text{amb}}}{R(T_{\max}) \theta_{JA}}}$$
  The test must reproduce the enclosure and neighboring heat loads under which that ceiling will be used.

- **Backdrive friction and impact dynamics**: By driving the actuator output shaft with the dynamometer load motor, the testbed measures the torque needed to backdrive the joint across speed, load, and temperature:
  $$\tau_{\text{ext}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}} \ddot{q} + \tau_{\text{fric}}$$
  The measured response establishes whether the transmission can yield under the intended external load and maps the friction term that @sec-body-actuation-regimes shows is not a constant. Contact qualification must additionally exercise the relevant compliance and impact conditions; the backdrive model alone does not predict tooth failure.

::: {#fig-02-real-motor-dyno-bench fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**An instrumented propulsion test stand**: An electric motor with its propeller, speed controller, and wiring secured at the top of the Airvolt test stand at the NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center in 2016, instrumented to collect data on the propulsion system under load. A stand like this measures what a data sheet only asserts, on the assembled drive under stated conditions. (Credit: Lauren Hughes, NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center, AFRC2016-0100-05, public domain.)" fig-alt="Photograph against a blue sky of a white angled pylon carrying a mounting plate at its top, with a two-blade propeller, an electric motor, a finned electronics box, and bundled orange and red wiring."}
![](images/jpg/fig02_real_motor_dyno_bench.jpg){width="85%"}
:::

Measurement can change the plant. A series current shunt lowers the supplied voltage, and an embedded temperature probe changes a local heat-flow path. These effects belong in the uncertainty budget along with sensor resolution, bandwidth, and clock alignment.

The sensor mechanisms in @sec-body-sensor-transduction also affect characterization. For example, velocity estimated from encoder samples uses the same backward difference:
  $$\dot{\theta}[k] \approx \frac{\theta[k] - \theta[k-1]}{\Delta t}$$
Its resolution-latency trade-off must therefore enter the reported uncertainty and response time. Vibration above the sensor's sampled bandwidth can likewise appear as slower motion:
  $$f_{\text{alias}} = |f_{\text{vib}} - k f_s|$$
The integer $k$ identifies the sampling-frequency multiple that folds the vibration into the observed band. Qualification must distinguish that measurement artifact from the motion used to establish the limit.

A limit means nothing without the context of its test. Every recorded limit states the payload, ambient temperature, supply voltage, enclosure state, firmware version, and concurrent computational workload of the run. A thermal time constant measured on an open bench does not transfer to the same actuator in a sealed fairing in sunlight, because enclosing the motor raises $\theta_{JA}$ and with it $\tau_{\text{th}} = \theta_{JA} C_{\text{th}}$, while the hotter ambient shrinks the margin below the insulation rating. A rail characterization that omits whether vision-language model inference [@brohan2023rt1; @brohan2023rt2] was running during motor stalls describes an idle board rather than the combined draw of full compute and peak torque.

### Statistical zero-failure bounds and lifecycle degradation {#sec-body-statistical-bounds}

```{python}
#| label: body-zero-failure-bound-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ ZERO-FAILURE BOUND ON LOADED STOPS (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the zero-failure paragraph in @sec-body-measuring-limits.
# │ Goal:    Bound the per-stop failure rate that n failure-free loaded stops
# │          support at 95 percent confidence.
# │ Show:    n = 3,000; -ln(0.05) = 2.996 (the rule of three); upper limit
# │          9.99e-4, about one stop in 1,000.
# │ How:     One-sided zero-failure bound p_upper = -ln(1 - c) / n.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import math
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_int, fmt_percent, check

class ZeroFailureBound:
    """Upper bound on the per-stop failure rate after n failure-free trials."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    n_stops = 3000  # category: illustrative (failure-free loaded stops)
    conf = 0.95  # category: chosen (one-sided confidence level)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    coef = -math.log(1 - conf)
    p_upper = coef / n_stops
    one_in = round(1 / p_upper, -2)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(coef - 2.9957) < 1e-4, f"Unexpected -ln(0.05): {coef}")
    check(abs(p_upper - 9.986e-4) < 1e-6, f"Unexpected upper bound: {p_upper}")
    check(one_in == 1000, f"Expected about one stop in 1,000: {one_in}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    n_str = fmt_int(n_stops)
    conf_pct_str = fmt_percent(conf, precision=0, style="prose")
    one_in_str = fmt_int(one_in)
```

The absence of a failure during testing bounds the failure rate statistically; it does not establish safety. If the mobile manipulator completes $n =$ `{python} ZeroFailureBound.n_str` loaded stops without a brownout or an overrun, the data support only a per-stop failure rate below roughly $3/n$ by the Rule of Three (@sec-evaluation-closed-loop-survival, @eq-eval-rule-of-three), about one stop in `{python} ZeroFailureBound.one_in_str` at `{python} ZeroFailureBound.conf_pct_str` confidence, and only if the trials are independent and stationary: one trial does not influence another, and the failure probability remains unchanged across trials.

Thermal history and wear can change the conditions between trials:

- **Thermal non-stationarity across consecutive trials**: Repeated stops heat the windings, changing resistance and the available torque response. Trials taken at different starting temperatures do not characterize the same operating condition.
- **Electrochemical impedance non-stationarity over the battery lifecycle**: Battery aging increases source resistance, reducing the voltage margin under a current step.
- **Mechanical backlash non-stationarity**: Transmission wear changes reversal response and tracking error, invalidating a limit measured on a less worn assembly.

These changes make characterization a standing obligation. **Lifecycle degradation**\index{Lifecycle degradation!definition} changes the conditions behind a limit, so its record must identify when recalibration or a reduced operating envelope is required.

### The six elements of a limit record {#sec-body-limit-record-schema}

```{python}
#| label: body-limit-records-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ THREE LIMIT RECORDS ON THE RUNNING MACHINE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @tbl-02-limit-record in @sec-body-measuring-limits, and the rail
# │          decision in @sec-body-archetype-matrix (hold-up, load, store).
# │ Goal:    Fill the six elements of a limit record for the credible
# │          deceleration, the drive torque ceiling, and the drive bus's
# │          converter lockout, and give the decision paragraph its hold-up
# │          values.
# │ Show:    a_brake 2.0 m/s^2, binding only where mu * phi >= 0.204, loaded
# │          to at most 368 kg, 100 mm protective clearance; drive torque
# │          ceiling >= 2.33 m/s^2 at 25 A (16.6 percent margin); converter
# │          lockout 33 V, 4.8 V sustained-load margin from a depleted pack;
# │          the permission rail is held up for 2.0 s (70 W, 2.025 F, 140 J)
# │          between 21.5 V and the 18 V dropout of its regulators, stated at
# │          the decision, not in the record.
# │ How:     mu_min = a_brake / g; store C = 2 P t / (V_low^2 - V_dropout^2)
# │          from RM.permission_rail_holdup_capacitance. The hold-up's basis
# │          (the longest commanded stop) is derived in @sec-enforcement.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import (
    fmt,
    fmt_mass,
    fmt_capacitance,
    fmt_length,
    fmt_latency,
    fmt_power,
    fmt_energy,
    fmt_voltage,
    fmt_acceleration,
    check,
    MarkdownStr,
)

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class LimitRecords:
    """The a_brake, drive-torque, and drive-bus lockout records for the running machine."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    a_brake = AISLE.a_brake  # category: illustrative (credible low tail, loaded, dry floor)
    m_loaded = RM.loaded_mass  # category: derived (upper bound, full tote rack)
    delta_margin = AISLE.delta_margin  # category: chosen (protective clearance)
    imu_name = RM.imu.name  # category: sourced (the machine's IMU part)
    v_dropout = RM.control_rail_dropout  # category: illustrative (permission-load regulator dropout)
    v_store_low = RM.control_rail_battery_low  # category: illustrative (lowest store charge voltage)
    holdup = RM.permission_rail_holdup  # category: chosen (permission-rail hold-up)
    p_rail = RM.permission_rail_load  # category: illustrative (permission-path load)
    c_store = RM.permission_rail_holdup_capacitance  # category: derived (store sized for the hold-up)
    v_uvlo = DriveBusIntegrity.v_uvlo  # category: sourced (48-to-24 V converter lockout)
    margin_low = DriveBusIntegrity.margin_low  # category: derived (depleted-pack margin under the sustained 70 A load)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    mu_min = (a_brake / ureg.standard_gravity).to("dimensionless").magnitude
    e_store = (p_rail * holdup).to(joule)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(a_brake.to(meter / second**2).magnitude - 2.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected a_brake: {a_brake}")
    check(abs(m_loaded.to(kilogram).magnitude - 368.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected loaded mass: {m_loaded}")
    check(abs(mu_min - 0.204) < 5e-4, f"Friction premise must be 0.204: {mu_min}")
    check(abs(delta_margin.to(ureg.millimeter).magnitude - 100.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected margin: {delta_margin}")
    check(abs(v_dropout.to(volt).magnitude - 18.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected dropout: {v_dropout}")
    check(abs(holdup.to(second).magnitude - 2.0) < 1e-9, f"Hold-up must be 2.0 s: {holdup}")
    check(abs(p_rail.to(ureg.watt).magnitude - 70.0) < 1e-9, f"Rail load must be 70 W: {p_rail}")
    check(abs(c_store.to(ureg.farad).magnitude - 2.025) < 5e-4, f"Store must be 2.025 F: {c_store}")
    check(abs(e_store.magnitude - 140.0) < 1e-9, f"Store energy must be 140 J: {e_store}")
    check(
        abs((0.5 * c_store * (v_store_low**2 - v_dropout**2)).to(joule).magnitude - e_store.magnitude) < 1e-6,
        "The store's usable energy between its lowest charge and dropout must equal load x hold-up.",
    )
    check(abs(margin_low.to(volt).magnitude - 4.8) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected depleted-pack margin: {margin_low}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    imu_name_str = MarkdownStr(imu_name)
    a_brake_str = fmt_acceleration(a_brake, unit=meter / second**2, precision=0)
    m_loaded_str = fmt_mass(m_loaded, unit=kilogram, precision=0)
    mu_min_str = fmt(mu_min, precision=3)
    delta_margin_str = fmt_length(delta_margin, unit=ureg.millimeter, precision=0)
    v_dropout_str = fmt_voltage(v_dropout, unit=volt, precision=0)
    holdup_str = fmt_latency(holdup, unit=second, precision=0)
    p_rail_str = fmt_power(p_rail, unit=ureg.watt, precision=0)
    c_store_str = fmt_capacitance(c_store, unit=ureg.farad, precision=3)
    v_store_low_str = fmt_voltage(v_store_low, unit=volt, precision=1)
    v_uvlo_str = fmt_voltage(v_uvlo, unit=volt, precision=0)
    margin_low_str = fmt_voltage(margin_low, unit=volt, precision=1)
    e_store_str = fmt_energy(e_store, unit=joule, precision=0)
```

The stopping and power calculations become usable by other layers only when their assumptions travel with their values. A **limit record**\index{Limit record!definition} carries those assumptions together with the evidence that supports the limit. The learned proposer in @sec-brain uses the limits to constrain candidate actions, while the independent permission path in @sec-nervous checks them before actuation. Recording a value does not certify it: the illustrative entries below still require measurements and uncertainty estimates before they can support operation. The six elements in @tbl-02-limit-record make that missing evidence visible for the mobile manipulator's credible deceleration, the drive torque ceiling that must support it, and the drive bus's undervoltage lockout.

Two of the elements are easily conflated. *Uncertainty describes what is not known about the measurement (observation noise, instrument tolerance, sensor bandwidth, and calibration drift); margin is the physical clearance the machine defends against what is not known.* The provenance element then says how far the value itself can be trusted. Every number that governs a machine is a direct measurement, a value derived from measurements through a stated model, a datasheet rating, or an illustrative example, and only the first two can support a safety margin or a timeout. A budget the designer sets, such as the protective clearance $\delta_{\text{margin}}$, is instead chosen, and it binds only once it is checked against the measured number it must fit (see the Reader Guide).

| Element         | What the record states                                                                                                                               | Credible deceleration $a_{\text{brake}}$                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Drive torque ceiling                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Drive-bus converter lockout                                                                                                                                            |
|:----------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Value**       | The value or empirical distribution, with its sample count and the tail percentiles it reports                                                       | `{python} LimitRecords.a_brake_str`, taken as the credible low tail of loaded stops; no samples yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | At least `{python} BrakingLimits.a_torque_str` from `{python} BrakingLimits.tau_wheel_str` per wheel; computed from datasheet values, no samples yet                                                                     | `{python} LimitRecords.v_uvlo_str` at the 48-to-24 V converter input; no samples on the assembled bus                                                                  |
| **Conditions**  | The context listed earlier under which it was established, plus the surface for any limit that depends on traction                                   | Loaded to at most `{python} LimitRecords.m_loaded_str`; $\mu\,\phi_{\text{drive}} \ge$ `{python} LimitRecords.mu_min_str`, so $\mu \ge$ `{python} BrakingLimits.mu_min_rated_str` at the hub motors' rated load share and never on the inspected floor ($\mu =$ `{python} BrakingLimits.mu_insp_str`); tip-over geometry not yet measured; usable powered braking and energy absorption; tires at commissioning wear | Drive current limit at `{python} BrakingLimits.i_max_str`; both driven wheels in traction; rotating mass within the `{python} BrakingLimits.m_rot_wheel_str` per-wheel bound; windings and bus within their rated ranges | Sustained coincident load on the 48 V bus; the permission path isolated on its held-up rail; drive power and physical stopping behavior require separate qualification |
