| **Uncertainty** | The measurement uncertainty of each instrument, with its observation point and bandwidth                                                             | Not established                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Datasheet tolerances only; the torque constant's tolerance is not published                                                                                                                                              | Not established                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Margin**      | The engineering margin separating the operating target from the breakdown threshold                                                                  | No justified deceleration margin yet; the chosen `{python} LimitRecords.delta_margin_str` protective clearance must be checked against the eventual uncertainty bound                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | At least `{python} BrakingLimits.torque_margin_pct_sym_str` above $a_{\text{brake}}$; none if the current limit falls to the rated `{python} BrakingLimits.i_rated_str`                                                  | `{python} LimitRecords.margin_low_str` from a depleted pack under sustained coincident load; transient minimum not established                                         |
| **Detector**    | The runtime check that catches an excursion while the machine runs, such as a phase-current sensor, an optical interrupter, or a supply-rail monitor | Deceleration monitor comparing commanded with measured deceleration from the wheel encoders and the `{python} LimitRecords.imu_name_str` inertial unit, on every stop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Drive saturation flag and measured phase current against the configured limit, read on every stop                                                                                                                        | Bus-voltage monitor flags undervoltage; the permission path selects a response whose power and mechanical premises still hold                                          |
| **Provenance**  | The evidence category and the instrument or model that produced the value                                                                            | Illustrative, from the base's class profile; to be replaced by loaded stopping trials                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Derived from the hub motor's datasheet; to be replaced by wheel-torque measurements at the current limit on a loaded braking trial                                                                                       | Converter datasheet; source resistance illustrative; to be replaced by a bus characterization under coincident load                                                    |

: **The limit record on the mobile manipulator**: The six elements of a limit record, filled in for the credible deceleration that sets the stopping distance, for the drive torque ceiling that must support it, and for the converter lockout that bounds the shared drive bus. None of the three yet has samples or an established uncertainty, and the provenance element names the measurement that would replace each. {#tbl-02-limit-record tbl-colwidths="[10,18,26,23,23]"}

The detector element matters most once the machine leaves the test stand, because operation can carry a limit outside the conditions under which it was established. The saturation duration against which the Schiaparelli lander's inertial unit had been accepted was such a limit, and the lander's loss in 2016 shows what follows when a limit's conditions are exceeded in operation and nothing downstream checks the result.

::: {#ws-body-2016-schiaparelli-imu-saturation .callout-war-story title="ExoMars Schiaparelli IMU saturation (2016)"}
**Context**: On October 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars Schiaparelli lander executed its atmospheric entry and descent toward the Martian surface, relying on an onboard Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) computer to fuse Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) gyroscopes with a Doppler radar altimeter [@esa2017schiaparelli].

**Mechanism**: About three minutes after atmospheric entry, the parachute inflated and set the lander oscillating. The IMU measured a pitch rate larger than expected and raised a saturation flag, which persisted longer than the 15 ms assumed when the unit was accepted. While the flag was set, the GNC software integrated the saturation threshold rate as though it were the true rate, although the lander was in reality oscillating, and its attitude estimate drifted by about $165^{\circ}$, nearly upside down. When the radar altimeter later returned valid slant ranges, the software projected them onto that attitude and computed a negative altitude. No onboard check tested that altitude for plausibility.

**Impact**: Taking the negative altitude as a valid estimate, the guidance logic released the parachute and backshell, fired the braking thrusters for $3\text{ seconds}$ instead of the planned $30\text{ seconds}$, and activated its on-ground systems as if it had landed. The lander was still about $3.7\text{ km}$ above the surface. It fell freely for about half a minute and struck the ground at about $150\text{ m/s}$ ($540\text{ km/h}$).

**Response**: The ESA inquiry board recommended robust sanity checks in the onboard software, among them that altitude cannot be negative and cannot change from $3.7\text{ km}$ to a negative value in one second, and a design that handles IMU saturation explicitly, for example by inhibiting IMU inputs during parachute deployment.

**Systems lesson**: A physical body cannot transcend the saturation ranges of its sensory transducers. When a sensor's physical limit (a gyroscope's rate ceiling or an accelerometer's dynamic range) is exceeded, a state estimator that integrates the saturated measurement as if it were valid drifts away from the physical state. The saturation duration against which the IMU had been accepted was a limit with conditions, and once descent exceeded them, no detector checked the estimate before it commanded an irreversible action.
:::

Measured and recorded one at a time, the five limits describe the body budget by budget, each under its own conditions. Which of them binds first depends on the machine and the command.

## Binding Budget Identification and Dominant Constraints {#sec-body-archetype-matrix}

A single command from the chunk policy to accelerate the loaded mobile manipulator spends from all five budgets at once. It rests on a camera frame that is already aging, it adds kinetic energy that the brakes must later remove, it accelerates reflected rotor inertia through the drive gearing, it deposits Joule heat in windings that shed it only over minutes, and it draws current from the rail that also feeds the application processor. @Tbl-02-cross-archetype-matrix sets the five budgets side by side, with the law that governs each, the assumption a policy trained in software makes about it, the machine class it binds first, and the design response and runtime invariant that answer it.

### Archetype-dependent binding constraints {#sec-body-binding-constraints}

The mobile manipulator carries two of the machine classes of @sec-boundary-three-classes on one chassis, a Class 1 base that binds first on momentum and stopping distance and a Class 2 arm that binds first on reflected inertia, contact stiffness, and holding heat.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The degraded limits recorded here bound the supervisor intervention thresholds derived in @sec-intervention-authority-transitions.
:::

Those class labels suggest where to look; the current maneuver determines which margin is smallest. Sustained holding can make the arm's thermal budget bind, whereas coincident drive and compute demand can exhaust the electrical margin almost immediately. @Tbl-02-cross-archetype-matrix connects each physical mechanism to the check it requires. The coupled calculation that follows selects the design response for the warehouse machine.

| Physical Budget / Factor            | Governing First Principle & Scaling Law                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Software Illusion vs. Hardware Ground Truth                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Primary Binding Class                                                                                                    | Systems Architect Takeaway & Runtime Invariant                                                                                                                         |
|:------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1. Measurement Freshness & Age**  | $\Delta t_{\text{fresh}} \le \frac{e_{\max}}{v_{\max}}$; $\delta \theta = \frac{2\pi}{2^n}$; end-to-end age measured from exposure                                                                                                                                                         | *Illusion:* High inference rate ($50\text{ Hz}$) guarantees real-time control. *Truth:* Age begins at exposure; encoder differentiation amplifies quantization noise; vibration harmonics alias into IMU attitude drift.                               | **Class 1 & 2:** Erodes clearance margins and destabilizes high-gain contact loops.                                      | Tag frames with hardware timestamps; enforce $t_{\text{age}} \le$ the budgeted age at motor registers; drop stale commands.                                            |
| **2. Momentum & Stopping Distance** | $d_{\text{stop}} = v\,\tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\text{brake}}} + \delta_{\text{loc}} + \delta_{\text{margin}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$; $m_{\text{eff}} = m + \sum_i \frac{N_i^2 J_{\text{rotor}, i}}{r_{\text{wheel}}^2}$                                                        | *Illusion:* Deceleration can be commanded instantaneously. *Truth:* Braking distance scales quadratically ($v^2$); retarding torque must decelerate reflected rotor inertia; the stopping system must absorb or dissipate energy.                      | **Class 1 (Mobility):** Primary constraint. Doubling speed quadruples the braking term.                                  | Solve clearance quadratic $v_{\max}(D_{\text{clear}}, \tau_{\text{delay}})$ on the safety microcontroller at the rate the stopping budget sets; clamp policy velocity. |
| **3. Actuator & Reflected Inertia** | $J_{\text{ref}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$; $\tau = K_t i_q$; $\tau_e = \frac{L}{R}$; $\frac{d\tau}{dt} \le \frac{K_t(V_{\text{bus}} - e_{\text{bemf}})}{L}$                                                                                                                                  | *Illusion:* Motor torque tracks policy tensors instantaneously. *Truth:* Current rise limits response; gearboxes square rotor inertia ($N^2$); high ratios increase resistance to rapid contact motion.                                                | **Class 2 (Manipulation):** Contact stiffness and reflected inertia constrain interaction.                               | Limit acceleration and torque slew; measure load-side response; select gearing and compliance for the qualified contact envelope.                                      |
| **4. Thermal Limits & Duty Cycle**  | $C_{\text{th}} \frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{\tau^2}{K_t^2} R(T) - \frac{\Delta T}{\theta_{JA}}$; $\tau_{\text{cont}} = K_t \sqrt{\frac{T_{\max} - T_{\text{amb}}}{R(T_{\max}) \theta_{JA}}}$                                                                                                      | *Illusion:* Motors deliver catalog peak torque continuously. *Truth:* Torque is current, current is heat ($P_{\text{loss}} \propto \tau^2$); continuous torque is limited by heat rejection at the characterized winding-temperature limit $T_{\max}$. | **Class 3 (Thermal) & Class 2:** Holding above the qualified continuous torque can overheat the windings.                | Run discrete $I^2 t$ thermal observers on the safety microcontroller; dynamically derate speed and torque when hotspot models approach limits.                         |
| **5. Electrical Power Integrity**   | $V_{\text{source}}-V_{\text{bus}}=R_{\text{bus}}I_{\text{source}}+L_{\text{bus}}\frac{dI_{\text{source}}}{dt}$; $C_{\text{bus}}\frac{dV_{\text{bus}}}{dt}=I_{\text{source}}-I_{\text{load}}$; $V_{\text{final}} = \sqrt{V_{\text{initial}}^2 + \frac{2 E_{\text{regen}}}{C_{\text{bus}}}}$ | *Illusion:* Power rails act as infinite, ideal voltage sources. *Truth:* Bus impedance collapses rail voltage under combined compute+motor bursts; braking surges overvoltage.                                                                         | **Class 1 & 3:** Peak multi-axis acceleration trips microcontroller brownout resets; regen surges destroy inverter FETs. | Enforce coordinated compute-actuation power budgets and $dI/dt$ limits; install dynamic brake choppers; characterize unpowered fallbacks.                              |

: **Cross-class physical constraint matrix**: The five budgets, the law that governs each, the assumption a software-trained policy makes about it, the class it binds first, and the runtime invariant that answers it. {#tbl-02-cross-archetype-matrix tbl-colwidths="[18,20,24,18,20]"}

### Cross-budget coupling and permission rail isolation {#sec-body-permission-rail-isolation}

```{python}
#| label: body-dvfs-throttle-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ THROTTLED PERCEPTION ON THE RUNNING MACHINE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the ranking of margins in @sec-body-archetype-matrix and the
# │          DVFS pitfall in @sec-body-fallacies-pitfalls.
# │ Goal:    Price the extra observation age a thermally throttled application
# │          processor adds, in travel at the machine's drive limit.
# │ Show:    the 22 ms backbone stretches to 33 ms at two-thirds clock, adding
# │          11 ms, or 16.5 mm at 1.5 m/s.
# │ How:     Backbone time AISLE.t_backbone scaled by the inverse clock ratio
# │          (compute-bound stage); added age times drive-limit speed (the v*tau
# │          term of @eq-body-stopping-distance).
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_latency, fmt_length, fmt_velocity, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class ThrottledPerception:
    """Travel cost of a DVFS-stretched perception stage on the running machine."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    v = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
    t_nominal = AISLE.t_backbone  # category: illustrative (vision backbone at full clock)
    clock_ratio = 2 / 3  # category: illustrative (DVFS clock as a fraction of full clock)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    t_throttled = (t_nominal / clock_ratio).to(millisecond)
    dt = (t_throttled - t_nominal).to(millisecond)
    d_extra = (v * dt).to(ureg.millimeter)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(v.to(meter / second).magnitude - 1.5) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected drive limit: {v}")
    check(abs(t_nominal.to(millisecond).magnitude - 22.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected backbone time: {t_nominal}")
    check(abs(t_throttled.magnitude - 33.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected throttled backbone time: {t_throttled}")
    check(abs(dt.magnitude - 11.0) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected added age: {dt}")
    check(abs(d_extra.magnitude - 16.5) < 1e-9, f"Unexpected added travel: {d_extra}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    v_str = fmt_velocity(v, unit=meter / second, precision=1)
    t_nominal_str = fmt_latency(t_nominal, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_throttled_str = fmt_latency(t_throttled, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    dt_str = fmt_latency(dt, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    d_extra_str = fmt_length(d_extra, unit=ureg.millimeter, precision=1)
```

An aggressive multi-axis acceleration spends these margins together. The drives draw current to accelerate links and reflected rotor inertia; the shared supply sags while winding losses accumulate heat. Bus input current must be characterized at the supply, since winding phase currents do not sum directly into battery current. The rail calculation already provides the coincident input step needed for this comparison.

On the 48 V drive bus the sustained electrical screen no longer binds first. The coincident step of \ref{nbk-body-dc-bus-power-integrity} sags a depleted pack at `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_battery_low_str` to `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_sag_low_str`, still `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.margin_low_str` above the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_uvlo_str` converter lockout. The tightest computed margin belongs instead to the stop itself: the drives clear the credible deceleration by only `{python} BrakingLimits.torque_margin_pct_str`, and only with their current limit at the motor peak, while the tip-over ceiling has no measured value at all. By comparison, the modeled heat-soaked arm joint retains `{python} ThermalBurst.t_hot_str` before a sustained threefold current burst reaches the insulation rating, and the body's stopping subtotal at the `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.v_str` drive limit leaves `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.remaining_str` for sensing and decision delay, a refined stop profile, and tracking uncertainty. These margins answer different questions in different units. Their comparison says where evidence is thinnest: the deceleration premise, which the stopping budget, the torque ceiling, and the unmeasured center of gravity all share.

Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) can reduce processor voltage and clock frequency to manage power and temperature. Its timing effect connects compute to physical clearance:
$$\text{SoC thermal dissipation} \longrightarrow \text{DVFS clock throttling} \longrightarrow \text{vision latency stretch} \longrightarrow \text{observation age inflation} \longrightarrow \text{pre-brake travel expansion} \longrightarrow \text{clearance margin erosion}$$
When drive motors and heavy perception heat the shared chassis, the operating system throttles GPU and CPU clocks. The vision backbone stretches from `{python} ThrottledPerception.t_nominal_str` to `{python} ThrottledPerception.t_throttled_str`, adding `{python} ThrottledPerception.dt_str` to observation age $t_{\text{age}}$ and so to the total pre-brake delay $\tau_{\text{delay}}$. At the `{python} ThrottledPerception.v_str` drive limit, this compute lag adds `{python} ThrottledPerception.d_extra_str` of blind travel to the stopping envelope before brakes engage. A software power optimization intended to protect silicon silently erodes the machine's physical clearance margin.

Passing the sustained screen does not make the shared bus a safe home for the permission path. The transient minimum is unqualified, and a supply fault such as a tripped fuse, a battery management disconnect, or a failed converter removes the bus altogether. Those cases motivate a **dual-rail architecture**. The shared bus continues to feed the high-current motor inverters and, through its converter, the application processor. A separate, reverse-blocked permission rail supplies the safety microcontroller, fieldbus transceivers, and spring-brake coils, so a shared-bus sag or fault need not also erase the controller responsible for the response.

For the selected `{python} LimitRecords.p_rail_str` permission load, a `{python} LimitRecords.c_store_str` supercapacitor store provides a modeled `{python} LimitRecords.e_store_str` of usable energy between its lowest charge voltage (`{python} LimitRecords.v_store_low_str`) and the dropout of the permission loads' regulators (`{python} LimitRecords.v_dropout_str`). That calculation sizes a `{python} LimitRecords.holdup_str` logic-and-coil hold-up interval. Component tolerances, conversion losses, and the actual load still require qualification. The interval is selected to cover the commanded response developed in @sec-enforcement-fallback-ladder.

Keeping that rail alive preserves the ability to detect undervoltage and request a response; it does not supply traction-drive braking torque. A powered stop additionally requires usable drive voltage, functioning inverters, and an energy-absorption path throughout deceleration. If the shared-rail fault removes those conditions, the applicable bound must come from the qualified unpowered response of @sec-body-unpowered-states. Holding-brake engagement cannot inherit the powered stopping distance merely because its coil controller survives. The resulting design decision is therefore conditional: isolate the permission path, then establish which physical stop remains available under each supply fault. @Sec-nervous-coupled-budget combines the supported stopping and timing premises into an execution lease; later enforcement and qualification must preserve these power premises.

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-body-fallacies-pitfalls}

Physical limits interact across subsystem boundaries. A design that meets each component budget can still fail when heat, timing, power, and motion change together.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Model inference time defines the measurement freshness latency.*

A team quantizes its vision backbone and reduces inference time from $30\text{ ms}$ to $10\text{ ms}$. The improvement shortens one stage, but the controller still acts on measurements that pass through exposure, readout, transfer, and operating-system queues. Commands then travel over the network fieldbus before the motor coil current rises to apply force. A $45\text{ ms}$ transport spike elsewhere in this chain can consume the clearance margin even when inference meets its benchmark. The engineering budget must measure the true "photon-to-torque" elapsed time from sensing to physical response and bound its tail, rather than declaring the loop real-time from model execution time alone.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Measure the true end-to-end photon-to-torque latency tail on synchronized hardware clocks; never certify real-time safety from neural network inference benchmarks alone.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Software step commands deliver instantaneous physical torque.*

A simulated policy issues piecewise-constant setpoints at $50\text{ Hz}$ and assumes the actuator acts as an ideal linear force source that follows each tensor update immediately. On physical hardware, however, an electric actuator is a dynamic system rather than an instantaneous converter from number to torque: it must build torque through Field-Oriented Control (FOC) current loops, where current rise is strictly bounded by stator winding inductance ($\tau_e = L/R$) and DC bus voltage headroom ($\frac{d\tau}{dt} \le \frac{K_t(V_{\text{bus}} - e_{\text{bemf}})}{L}$). Furthermore, the transmission gearhead amplifies rotor inertia quadratically ($J_{\text{ref}} = N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$), acting as an aggressive mechanical low-pass filter on joint acceleration.

When a policy demands abrupt changes, some motor effort accelerates the rotor rather than the external link, and transmission compliance can turn the mismatch into oscillation. Contact loads then depend on the reflected inertia, friction, and compliance of the assembled joint. Repeated high-current corrections also consume the thermal budget through $P_{\text{loss}} = \frac{\tau^2}{K_t^2} R$. Setpoint shaping must therefore be checked against delivered response, rather than accepted because the command sequence is numerically smooth.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Bound acceleration and torque slew using measured actuator response, include electrical current rise and reflected inertia in the model, and qualify the chosen transmission and controller for the intended contact task.

:::

```{python}
#| label: body-catalog-derating-calc
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ INSTALLED CONTINUOUS TORQUE AGAINST THE CATALOG RATING (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: the datasheet pitfall in @sec-body-fallacies-pitfalls.
# │ Goal:    Show how far the continuous-torque ceiling falls when a motor
# │          rated at a 25 C test ambient runs at the enclosed 40 C of the
# │          thermal notebooks, and again if installation doubles theta_JA.
# │ Show:    ambient alone: sqrt(100/115) = 0.933, 6.7 percent lower; with
# │          theta_JA doubled as well: 0.659, 34.1 percent lower.
# │ How:     tau_cont proportional to sqrt((T_max - T_amb) / theta_JA), same
# │          motor and ceiling; T_max from CopperResistanceRise, T_amb from
# │          ThermalBurst.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_temperature, fmt_percent, check

class CatalogDerating:
    """Continuous-torque ceiling at installed ambient and thermal resistance, relative to the catalog."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    t_max = CopperResistanceRise.t_ceiling  # category: chosen (engineering ceiling, declared once)
    t_amb_catalog = ureg.Quantity(25.0, ureg.degC).to(ureg.kelvin)  # category: illustrative (catalog test ambient)
    t_amb_installed = ThermalBurst.t_amb  # category: illustrative (enclosed ambient of the thermal notebooks)
    theta_factor = 2.0  # category: illustrative (installed theta_JA relative to the catalog heat sink)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    ambient_share = (((t_max - t_amb_installed) / (t_max - t_amb_catalog)).to("dimensionless").magnitude) ** 0.5
    both_share = ambient_share / theta_factor**0.5

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(ambient_share - 0.9325) < 1e-4, f"Unexpected ambient-only share: {ambient_share}")
    check(abs(both_share - 0.6594) < 1e-4, f"Unexpected combined share: {both_share}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    t_max_str = fmt_temperature(t_max, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    t_amb_catalog_str = fmt_temperature(t_amb_catalog, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    t_amb_installed_str = fmt_temperature(t_amb_installed, unit=ureg.degC, precision=0)
    ambient_loss_pct_str = fmt_percent(1 - ambient_share, precision=1, style="prose")
    both_loss_pct_str = fmt_percent(1 - both_share, precision=1, style="prose")
```

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Treating isolated component datasheets as operational system guarantees.*

An engineer uses a motor's catalog continuous torque rating or a sensor's nominal accuracy specification to set policy action limits. The motor rating carries the vendor's test conditions (@sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles), a motor mounted to a large heat sink in free air at a test ambient such as `{python} CatalogDerating.t_amb_catalog_str`, not those of a sealed joint inside an unventilated limb on a chassis that also carries a `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.p_soc_str` application processor. In reality, continuous torque is limited by thermal dissipation up to the winding's temperature ceiling $T_{\max}$:
$$\tau_{\text{cont}} = K_t \sqrt{\frac{T_{\max} - T_{\text{amb}}}{R(T_{\max}) \theta_{JA}}}$$
With the `{python} CatalogDerating.t_max_str` engineering ceiling, moving the motor from a `{python} CatalogDerating.t_amb_catalog_str` test ambient into the `{python} CatalogDerating.t_amb_installed_str` enclosure of the thermal examples costs `{python} CatalogDerating.ambient_loss_pct_str` of continuous torque by itself. Because the ceiling scales as $1/\sqrt{\theta_{JA}}$, losing the catalog's heat sink and free airflow matters more: if installation doubles $\theta_{JA}$, the two effects together remove `{python} CatalogDerating.both_loss_pct_str` of the catalog rating. If the planner treats the catalog number as its operational limit, stator copper losses ($P_{\text{loss}} = \frac{\tau^2}{K_t^2} R$) will exceed the thermal dissipation capacity and age the slot insulation faster than its thermal class allows. Similarly, an IMU or optical encoder tested on an isolated bench exhibits far higher variance, quantization noise, and vibration aliasing when bolted to a vibrating mobile chassis. Operational limits must derive from empirical limit records measured on the fully assembled machine under compound operational stress.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Calibrate actuator continuous torque ceilings and sensor noise profiles on fully assembled, enclosed hardware across the entire operational temperature envelope rather than copying open-bench catalog numbers into planner configuration files.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Treating dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) as a transparent software optimization.*

The mobile manipulator's drive motors heat the shared chassis until its application processor triggers dynamic voltage and frequency scaling\index{Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling} (DVFS) to avoid junction overtemperature. The power manager treats the slower clock as a local efficiency decision, yet the throttled backbone adds `{python} ThrottledPerception.dt_str` to the observation age, and at the `{python} ThrottledPerception.v_str` drive limit that becomes `{python} ThrottledPerception.d_extra_str` of blind travel (@sec-body-permission-rail-isolation). The silicon is protected, and a stopping margin validated at full clock no longer holds. Thermal telemetry must therefore inform the motion budget, with travel speed reduced when processor throttling increases the time needed to perceive and respond.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Feed SoC thermal and clock-frequency telemetry directly into the motion safety monitor, dynamically derating maximum travel speed whenever compute throttling inflates perception age.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Scaling operational velocity without recalculating quadratic braking distances and thermal dissipation.*

Repeated high-current braking heats the motor windings, so a stop the mobile manipulator survives once at a raised operating speed may exceed its allowable thermal duty cycle (the thermal capacity budget) when repeated through a shift, on top of the quadratic growth in braking travel that Case 3 in @fig-02-stopping-distance shows at `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.v_fast_str`. A higher operating speed requires a new stopping-distance calculation and a thermal assessment of repeated maneuvers before the planner can safely treat that speed as available.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Treat operating speed as an admission parameter that re-evaluates both quadratic stopping envelopes and multi-cycle thermal accumulation before granting velocity increases.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Compute accelerators and motor inverters operate on independent, ideal power rails.*

On the mobile manipulator, a heavy inference burst coincides with the drive motors pushing the base over the cage-door threshold. Budgeted separately, each load fits its own supply rating, and neither budget sees the other. On the shared `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_bus_nom_str` drive bus, however, the combined `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.di_str` step across the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.r_bus_str` source resistance produces a `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.dv_str` sustained drop, spending almost half of the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.headroom_low_str` that separates a depleted pack from the `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.v_uvlo_str` lockout of the converter feeding the application processor, before inductance and capacitor depletion deepen the transient. A step of `{python} DriveBusIntegrity.i_cross_str`, or the same step through a source whose resistance has grown with age and cold, crosses the lockout and resets the processor. Had the safety microcontroller shared that supply, the same brownout would have reset it too while the machine carried active momentum, leaving the base and arm to the unpowered states of @sec-body-power-integrity instead of a commanded stop. Separate software budgets for compute and actuation ignore their physical reliance on a shared electrical supply. Power qualification must test coincident peak loads from a depleted battery, with the controller that stops the machine on its own held-up rail (@sec-body-archetype-matrix).

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Isolate the permission logic and brake releases, then qualify both their hold-up and the physical stopping response under coincident motor and compute load at minimum battery state of charge. A powered stop also requires the drive rail and energy-absorption path to remain usable.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Passing isolated single-variable bench tests guarantees physical survival under compound operational stress.*

A robot arm passes a maximum-payload trial in a $20^\circ\text{C}$ air-conditioned laboratory and an empty-gripper trial in a $45^\circ\text{C}$ thermal chamber. Neither test establishes its ability to carry that maximum payload in the hotter environment while running on a depleted battery. Under these combined conditions, the heavy physical load raises resistive winding losses, the hotter surroundings reduce the system's ability to reject that heat, and the lower supply voltage leaves less headroom above back-EMF, capping speed and current slew. Consequently, each subsystem can approach its failure limit much sooner than the separate, isolated trials suggest. Qualification must therefore exercise realistic combinations of payload, temperature, and battery condition on the assembled machine, rather than treating individual test passes as evidence about the combined conditions.

**Architect's Countermeasure**: Test boundary envelopes under worst-case simultaneous physical stress—maximum payload, elevated ambient temperature, depleted battery, and high-frequency actuation—to catch multi-budget coupling failures.

:::

## Summary {#sec-body-summary}

The five budgets turn a requested maneuver into constraints on measurement age, stopping distance, delivered torque, winding temperature, and supply voltage. Their coupling determines the hardware decision. On the warehouse machine's 48 V drive bus, the sustained electrical screen passes even from a depleted pack, and the thinnest evidence sits under the credible deceleration: its drive-torque margin is small and depends on the configured current limit, its traction premise depends on how much weight the driven wheels carry, and its tip-over premise has no measured center of gravity behind it. Isolating and holding up the permission path still preserves control availability through supply faults and unqualified transients, but qualifying its physical response requires establishing the drive power or unpowered braking behavior available during the fault.

The limit record carries each value with its conditions, uncertainty, margin, detector, and provenance. On the mobile manipulator at its `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.v_str` drive limit, the body's stopping terms spend `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.total_3_str` of the `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance. The remaining `{python} BodyStoppingBudget.remaining_str` is a design budget for sensing and computation, the refined stop profile, and tracking uncertainty. Those illustrative values organize the next engineering decisions; measurements on the assembled machine must establish the limits that operation can rely on.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="The physical body and invariant budgets"}
* **Age begins at physical transduction**: The freshness budget spans sensing through physical response, and an end-to-end percentile is not the sum of stage percentiles. Preserve capture time, account for remaining response delay, and refuse a proposal whose evidence will be too old when the actuator responds.
* **Speed sets the stopping envelope**: Pre-brake travel grows linearly with delay and braking travel quadratically with speed. The clearance quadratic yields a candidate speed ceiling only while the current state, credible deceleration, and selected stopping mechanism satisfy its premises, and the credible deceleration itself must fit under the traction, tip-over, and drive-torque ceilings.
* **Gearing trades torque for reflected inertia**: Gearboxes multiply torque by the ratio but reflected rotor inertia by its square. Delivered response also depends on current rise, voltage headroom, friction, and compliance, so command acceptance does not establish physical tracking.
* **Thermal history limits available torque**: Copper loss grows quadratically with current, and winding resistance rises with temperature. A burst schedule must respect its hottest transient, not only average power; reducing holding current also requires a feasible way to support the load.
* **The supply rail is shared**: Motor inverters and application processors draw from a common DC bus, where coincident current steps spend the headroom between a depleted battery and the converter's undervoltage lockout, and unclamped regenerative stops can destroy inverter switching stages. An isolated, capacitor-held rail keeps the permission path available during a main-rail brownout. A controlled stop still requires sufficient braking energy, torque, and clearance; otherwise the machine depends on its qualified unpowered response.
* **A limit is a record, not a number**: A limit governs a decision only with its conditions, uncertainty, margin, detector, and provenance, and it lapses when lifecycle degradation (thermal resistance rise, battery impedance growth, gear backlash wear) alters those conditions.
:::

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From body limits to brain proposals"}
The **limit records** state how old an observation may be, how far the loaded base travels before stopping, and how much torque, heat, and electrical demand a maneuver may impose under declared conditions. A learned proposer must supply useful actions within those constraints. @Sec-brain examines what its models can produce, how long a new trajectory chunk takes, and how quickly its supporting observations age. Those proposer limits join the body's limits in @sec-nervous, where the permission path derives execution leases and collects the timing assumptions in the handoff record. The Brain supplies proposals; the permission path decides how long any proposal may drive the actuators.
:::
